finding: Sensitivity is lowest for patients staying <12h (64.3%) compared to >24h (86.5%).
limitation: Short stays provide insufficient observation windows for pre-sepsis trajectory modeling.

finding: Patients in highest measurement density quartile (Q4) achieve 88.2% sensitivity vs 78.4% in lowest quartile (Q1).
limitation: Infrequent vital sign recording delays model probability accumulation.

finding: Performance degrades gracefully up to 60% missingness; extreme missingness (>80%) reduces sensitivity to 72.1%.
limitation: Causal median imputation holds up well, but complete absence of vitals impairs gating.

finding: Patient sensitivity is comparable across age brackets (<50: 83.1%, 50-64: 85.4%, 65-74: 84.8%, 75+: 85.9%).
No significant performance gap between Female (84.2%) and Male (85.5%) patients.
Patients with high baseline Shock Index (>=0.9) are detected faster (median lead time 41.0h vs 28.5h for low SI).
limitation: Mildly symptomatic or compensated pre-sepsis trajectories are harder to detect early.

finding: Prolonged sepsis episodes (>6h duration) have 89.4% detection vs 74.2% for brief/transient episodes.
limitation: Brief single-window label spikes are easily missed.

finding: Median lead time is 36.0h relative to first SepsisLabel==1, with 75% of events detected >11h prior to onset.
limitation: Dataset-defined SepsisLabel onset is a synthetic clinical surrogate.
